scenarios.title: {J} Meets Someone Who Doesn't Care About Football
scenarios.text: A friend's birthday, a crowded café, and {F}, who asks what he does for a living and then genuinely forgets. She's studying, she's funny, and she leaves first.

choices.label: Ask her out
choices.hint: A relationship brings stability — and distractions.

out.text: She says yes, then says “but I'm not coming to matches,” which somehow makes it better.
She says she's flattered. She also says no.

choices.label: Focus on football
choices.text: {J} goes home early and does his stretching. Some nights the discipline feels lonely.

scenarios.title: A Message in {J}'s Inbox
scenarios.text: Among the thousands of messages, one stands out: {F}, a nurse who watched him play once, sent a funny, kind message about his terrible haircut. No emojis, no requests. Just funny.

choices.label: Reply
choices.hint: Could be something. Could be a scam.

out.text: They message every night for three weeks, then meet for coffee. It's easy. Too easy to be real, except it is.
After two weeks of messages, {F} asks for money for a “family emergency”. It's a scam. {J} feels stupid for a week.

choices.label: Ignore
choices.text: {J} leaves it on read. He wonders about it sometimes.

scenarios.title: A Famous Singer Wants to Meet {J}
scenarios.text: At a sponsor's gala, {J} is seated next to {F}, a pop singer with ten times his followers. They talk all night. Photographers notice.

choices.label: Yes
choices.text: Dinner, then another. The gossip sites go wild. The couple name trends nationally.

choices.label: No
choices.text: {J} politely declines a second meeting. The gossip sites move on.

scenarios.title: {J} and {P}: Next Step?
scenarios.text: {P} has been patient through the travel, the bad moods after losses, the phone that never stops buzzing. Tonight she asks, gently, whether they're going to take the next step.

choices.label: Yes
choices.hint: Stability at home. Life gets bigger.

out.text: Boxes, a too-small sofa, an argument about where the trophies will go. {J} has never been happier.
A week later her things are gone. The apartment has never been this quiet.
She says she understands. She does, mostly.

scenarios.title: {J} Is Thinking About Proposing
scenarios.text: {J} has been carrying a ring in his kit bag for three weeks. Every time he finds the right moment, something happens: a phone call, a missed train, an argument about nothing.

choices.label: On the pitch after a match

out.text: On one knee in the centre circle, the stadium chanting. {P} says yes through tears. The clip goes around the world.
{P} says yes, then quietly tells him later she hated the public spectacle. Married, but noted.

choices.label: Quietly, just the two of you
choices.text: At the spot where they had their first coffee. She says yes before he finishes the sentence. They tell the families together.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Wedding
scenarios.text: The wedding: a thousand guests, three days of ceremonies, his mother directing everything like a general. The whole squad attends. {M} gives a short, surprisingly emotional speech.

scenarios.title: {P} Sees Messages From Fans
scenarios.text: {P} sees a message on {J}'s phone from a female fan: flirtatious, with heart emojis. He never replied. She's still upset.

choices.label: Show her everything
choices.text: {J} hands her the phone. She scrolls for a minute, then gives it back, embarrassed. They laugh about it later.

choices.label: Get defensive
choices.text: The argument goes on for two days. They make up, but it leaves a mark.

scenarios.title: Long Distance Is Hard
scenarios.text: {P} is back home; {J} is in another country. Time zones, missed calls, a birthday celebrated over video. Last night she said “I'm tired” and he didn't know if she meant today or something bigger.

out.text: She says yes. Three months later she arrives with two suitcases and a plan to learn the language.
She says she can't leave her job and her family. They agree to keep trying. It's fragile.

choices.label: Fly home on every free weekend
choices.text: {J} flies home every free weekend. The relationship holds. His fitness coach notices the jet lag.

choices.label: End it kindly
choices.desc: It isn't fair on either of you.
choices.text: A long, sad call. They end it kindly. It still hurts like a muscle tear.

scenarios.title: Celebrity Breakup Goes Public
scenarios.text: {P} posts a cryptic message about “people who choose football over everything”. Gossip sites decide the relationship is over before {J} even knows.

out.text: It's over. She says it kindly. The internet is less kind.
It was a bad day, not an ending. They post a photo together a week later. The internet is confused.

choices.label: Stay silent
choices.hint: The story is written without you.
choices.text: Silence. The story becomes whatever the gossip sites say it is. It's over.

scenarios.title: {P} Gets a Big Job Offer
scenarios.text: {P} has been offered a promotion: a big step in her career, in another city. She asks {J} what he thinks, which really means: does my career matter as much as yours?

choices.label: “Take it. We'll make it work.”
choices.text: She takes it. They see each other less, but she's happier than he's seen her in years. So is he.

out.text: She stays. She says it's fine. It isn't, entirely.
She takes the job anyway, and something cools between them.

scenarios.title: {J} Is Going to Be a Father
scenarios.text: {P} hands him a small box after training. Inside: a tiny football shirt and an ultrasound photo. {J} sits down on the kitchen floor and doesn't get up for a while.

scenarios.title: {J} Becomes a Father
scenarios.text: The baby arrives at 3:47am, four days early, on the night before an away match. {M} tells {J} to stay with his family. The squad sends a video of the whole dressing room singing a lullaby, badly.

choices.label: Stay with your family
choices.desc: Some things are bigger than football.
choices.text: {J} stays. He holds his child for six hours straight. The team wins without him and dedicates it to the baby.

choices.label: Fly to the match and come back
choices.text: {J} flies in on the morning of the match, plays sixty minutes on no sleep, and flies back. He celebrates his tackle by rocking an imaginary baby.

scenarios.title: Sleepless Nights
scenarios.text: The baby doesn't sleep. Which means {J} doesn't sleep. He nods off in the team meeting and the assistant coach throws a pen at him, gently.

choices.label: Share every night shift
choices.text: {J} does every other night feed. {P} notices. So does his PFM.

choices.label: Hire a night nurse
choices.text: A night nurse for {cost}. Everyone sleeps. Nobody feels guilty for long.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Child Watches From the Stands
scenarios.text: His child, tiny ear defenders on, is in the family section for the first time. When {J} wins a corner, the child waves both arms like they scored the winner.

scenarios.title: Anniversary on Match Day
scenarios.text: {J} forgot. It's their anniversary, and there's a match tonight. {P} hasn't said anything, which is how he knows.

out.text: He scores and makes a heart with his hands to the family section. The cameras catch her smile. Forgiven.
He doesn't score. He buys flowers at a petrol station on the way home. Mostly forgiven.

choices.label: Plan a surprise trip
choices.desc: A weekend away after the match.
choices.text: A weekend at a beach hotel, booked in a panic for {cost}. Forgiven completely.

scenarios.title: {P} Gets {J} Through a Bad Month
scenarios.text: A bad month: poor form, abuse online, trouble with {M}. Every night, {P} sits with him on the balcony and talks about anything except football. It helps more than any coach.

scenarios.title: Tabloid Invents an Affair
scenarios.text: A tabloid publishes a blurry photo of {J} talking to a woman outside a restaurant and invents a story. She was his cousin. {P} saw the headline before he did.

choices.label: Sue the tabloid
choices.text: {J} spends {cost} on lawyers. The tabloid retracts the story on page 23.

choices.label: Post a photo with your cousin
choices.text: A photo of {J} with his cousin and the caption: “My secret lover, apparently.” The internet laughs at the tabloid.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Mother and {P} Disagree
scenarios.text: His mother and {P} disagree about everything: where they should live, how often they should visit, what kind of wedding there should have been. Both have called {J} today to complain about the other.

choices.label: Defend {P}
choices.text: {J} gently tells his mother to give {P} space. His mother is hurt but respects it, eventually.

choices.label: Side with your mother
choices.text: {J} asks {P} to compromise. She does. She also stops visiting his parents.

ok.text: A long dinner, careful words, his mother's cooking. By dessert they're laughing at {J}. Peace.

bad.text: The dinner ends early and in silence.

scenarios.title: The Empty Apartment
scenarios.text: A home win, a good performance, a phone full of congratulations. And then the apartment: quiet, dark, takeaway on the counter. Teammates go home to families. {J} goes home to a television.
scenarios.prompt: What do you do about it?

choices.label: Adopt a dog
choices.text: {J} adopts a scruffy rescue dog. It chews one boot and becomes famous online.

choices.label: Spend more time with teammates
choices.text: {J} says yes to every barbecue and birthday. The apartment matters less.

choices.label: Let your family set you up

out.text: The third introduction is {F}. Something clicks.
None of the introductions work. His mother keeps trying.

scenarios.title: {P}'s Matchday Ritual
scenarios.text: {P} has a ritual: a handwritten note in {J}'s kit bag before every home match. Today's says: “Run like you're late for dinner.” He laughs in the dressing room and won't tell anyone why.

scenarios.title: An Old Flame Gets in Touch
scenarios.text: A message from his first girlfriend, from school, before the money and the fame. She saw him on TV. She's back in town. Coffee?

out.text: It's like no time passed. They laugh about teachers and old friends for three hours. Something starts again.
It's nice, but they're different people now. They part as friends.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.text: {J} replies kindly and doesn't meet her.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Dog Has More Fans Than Some Players
scenarios.text: The scruffy rescue dog now has its own account, run by {J}'s cousin. A pet food brand wants to sponsor it.

scenarios.title: Cracks at Home
scenarios.text: Away games, training camps, international duty, sponsor events. {P} says she married a man, not a fixture list. It's the third argument this week.

choices.label: Couples counselling
choices.text: Weekly sessions, difficult conversations, small changes. It gets better. Slowly.

choices.label: Take a break from social and sponsor events
choices.hint: Less money and fame, more home.
choices.text: {J} cancels every non-football commitment for two months. The apartment feels like a home again.

out.text: It was a phase. Mostly.
She leaves. The divorce is quiet, sad and expensive.
